title: One box gone
venue: Arthur's site · the coastal weeklies · from 2017 the aggregator
logline: Monday. The end of the summer. One lockbox gone from one door — the strip doesn't know why and won't guess. Eleven doors. The empty knob drawn as carefully as the box was.

panels.composition: Main street, late August. WOOD and BARNABY II. A door with a bare knob where a lockbox hung all summer. A pale rectangle on the paint.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink, a house door with a bare doorknob and a pale rectangle on the paint where a lockbox hung, a man and a small dog on the sidewalk

panels.composition: The knob. The rectangle. The screw holes.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink, close-up of a doorknob with a pale unpainted rectangle beside it and two small screw holes

panels.composition: Wood looking at the door. Not her porch — a different door. The strip is careful: not hers.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink, a man looking at a house door from the sidewalk, no words
image.notes: Not Chloe's parents' house. A different door. The strip is explicit in composition: the wrong porch shape.

panels.composition: Walking on. Eleven boxes on eleven doors behind him. The strip counted twelve in July. It counts eleven now and says nothing.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink, a man and a small three-legged dog walking down a street of old houses with key lockboxes on eleven of twelve doors, no words

art.line: razor-sharp brush and ink; the pup's weight learned; Sundays wet-on-wet
art.palette: dailies: ink and one tone. Sundays: gray-green, fog, rust, bruised dusk

notes: Eleven. Not her door. Why: not known.
